headline: Buffalo National River Permits and Water Levels
reservation: While the Buffalo National River has no general entry fee, most developed campgrounds require reservations via recreation.gov; first-come sites are limited. Concessionaire permits are required for commercial float trips; distinguish between self-shuttled and outfitter-supported river access. Always check the official NPS river gauge before arrival as levels fluctuate rapidly.

days.title: Bluffs and Boxley Wildlife

stops.name: Lost Valley Trail
stops.detail: Walk through a box canyon to see Eden Falls and natural bridges, monitoring for slippery limestone surfaces.

stops.name: Boxley Valley Historic District
stops.detail: Observe the resident elk herd in the meadows during the early morning hours from designated roadside pullouts.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; winding mountain roads require slow speeds
days.note: Lost Valley parking is frequently at capacity by 10 AM on weekends; early arrival is suggested.

days.title: The Buffalo National River Float

stops.name: Steel Creek to Kyle's Landing
stops.detail: Paddle a scenic stretch of the upper river beneath massive bluffs, provided water levels are sufficient.

stops.name: Roark Bluff
stops.detail: View one of the most photographed limestone formations along the river corridor from the Steel Creek access.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for shuttle logistics; actual river time is 4–6 hours
days.note: The upper river is often too low for floating in late summer; be prepared to switch to the middle or lower river sections.

days.title: Scenic Overlooks and Historic Towns
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM heading south on Hwy 7

stops.name: Rotary Ann Overlook
stops.detail: Take in a 180-degree view of the Ozark National Forest from Arkansas's first rest area.

stops.name: Buffalo River Trail at Pruitt
stops.detail: Hike a portion of the trail near the historic Pruitt Bridge for river views and forest immersion.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours; Highway 7 involves steep grades and sharp curves
days.note: Cellular navigation is unreliable in the deep hollows; carry a physical topographic map.

intel.title: River Access and Trailhead Limits
intel.text: Kyle's Landing and Steel Creek parking areas can fill early during peak floating season. Heavy boat trailers can make maneuvering difficult in small gravel lots.

intel.title: Remote Hollow Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service is non-existent in Boxley Valley and most river canyons. Emergency phones are available at some ranger stations but should not be relied upon for daily logistics.

intel.title: Gateway Gas Stops
intel.text: Jasper and Harrison are the primary fuel hubs. Do not enter the backroads toward Erbie or Ponca with less than a quarter tank.

intel.title: Spring Runoff and Fall Peaks
intel.text: Spring rains cause rapid river rises; avoid gravel bars if storms are forecast upstream. Fall foliage typically arrives in mid-to-late October.

intel.title: Cave and Trail Closures
intel.text: Some caves are closed to protect bat populations from White-nose Syndrome. Check the NPS 'Current Conditions' page for trail washouts after heavy rain.

plan.arrival: Fly into Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) or Waynesville (TBN) and drive approximately 90–120 minutes. Harrison serves as the best supply point for coolers and river gear.
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle works for main highways, but a high-clearance SUV is recommended for reaching remote trailheads like Erbie or Kyles Landing which involve steep gravel roads.
plan.goldenHour: Steel Creek Overlook; sunrise adds mist to the river valley in spring and fall.
